title.narrative: Life-saving Response to Unaddressed Nutrition and Displacement needs in Abergele/ Ychlla woredas of Tigray region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtSave the Children (SC)’s proposed integrated multi-sectoral emergency interventions, including multi-purpose cash transfers (MPCT), WASH, emergency shelter/non-food items (ES/NFI), and health intervention, are designed to provide life-saving assistance and build resilience among the most vulnerable populations in Abergele/Yechilla woreda of Tigray region. Abergele/Yechilla woreda is among the woredas in Tigray region that faces heightened vulnerability due to multiple factors, including the effects of protracted wars, drought, crop infestations, and limited humanitarian support. These incidents have resulted in mass displacement, loss of livelihoods, compromised food access, and disrupted essential services, leading to significant food insecurity among the population, particularly affecting the nutrition status of women and children under five.ltbrgtThrough the proposed health intervention, the project will provide immediate lifesaving and preventive services by deploying surge teams to the most marginalized health facilities with high malnutrition caseloads and poor maternal, child health, and outreach services. Additionally, the program will support health facility rehabilitation, including providing life-saving essential medicines, supplies, and equipment, and assisting the woreda health office in minor rehabilitation of damaged health facilities to ensure the provision of basic healthcare services to both host and IDP communities. Similarly, to address critical potable and safe water needs, the project will rehabilitate damaged water schemes and provide water treatment chemicals to prevent waterborne diseases like cholera.ltbrgtDue to heavy rains and a lack of shelter and essential household items among IDP households, the program aims to provide shelter/NFI support to an estimated 150 female-headed and elderly Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). Additionally, a multi-purpose cash transfer will be distributed to an estimated 200 vulnerable households, including female/child-headed households and survivors of Gender-Based Violence (GBV). This intervention will complement General Food Distribution, supplementary, and therapeutic feeding programs provided by other partners, contributing to improved nutritional status, decreased morbidity and mortality due to malnutrition, and addressing critical household needs such as rent, consumables, and medication.ltbrgtBy implementing these interventions, the project aims to save lives, reduce suffering, and create a foundation for long-term recovery in Abergele/Yechilla woreda.ltbrgtlt/pgt
